History of Present Illness:
___ y/o F with chronic abdominal pain and a prior unintentional 
overdose on Tylenol, c/b acute liver injury, pancreatitis and c. 
diff colitis, who was transferred from the medicine service, 
where she was initially admitted on ___ for medical 
stabilization after taking 20 morphine tablets over a
period of one day. Pt was recently discharged from ___ on 
___ after a two day admission for worsening abdominal pain and 
associated nausea and vomiting. Her symptoms were thought to be 
secondary to endometriosis vs. stable hemorrhagic cyst, as well 
as mild recurrent pancreatitis vs. gastritis. For pain, she was 
treated with 4mg IV q3h with good results, and discharged on 
morphine ___ po q6h (60 tablets). Psychiatry saw the pt 
during this
admission and referred her to the partial hospitalization 
program at ___ for help with coping skills 
around her chronic pain. She was also discharged on lorazepam 
1mg q6h for anxiety.
.
Pt called her PCP and ___ clinic on ___ informing them that 
her mother had taken away her pain medications and requesting 
new prescriptions for lorazepam and oxycontin. On ___, she was 
admitted to the ICU with tachycardia to the 150s in the setting 
of a narcotic overdose. She reported to the psychiatry team on 
___ that she had an acute exacerbation of abdominal pain and 
took at least twenty morphine tablets over the course of one 
day. Her mother found her lethargic the following morning and 
called EMS, who transferred her to the ED. At the time she 
admitted to poor judgment but stated that did not intentionally 
overdose and had no thoughts of harming herself. 
.
Psychiatric Course: Pt was followed by the psychiatry consult 
service from ___ to ___. She was started on Remeron 7.5mg 
qhs for depression and insomnia. The team recommended 
discontinuing lorazepam, as there was no indication for this 
medication and she had demonstrated some substance abuse risk. 
Pt initially denied that the overdose was intentional, but later 
acknowledged that she was feeling depressed and hopeless and 
took the pills in an effort to ""get away from it all,"" although 
not specifically to kill herself. On the evening of ___, she 
reportedly took the bag of IV morphine into the bathroom and 
used all of it at once. The team recommended psychiatric 
hospitalization for evaluation and diagnostic clarification in 
the setting of limited coping skills, poor insight and 
judgement, and concern for opiate abuse. 
.
Medical Course: Pt was continued on morphine 4mg IV q3h for pain 
management. The chronic pain service was consulted and they 
recommended starting gabapentin 300mg TID and gradually weaning 
off oxycodone. At time of transfer to ___, pt was on 
oxycodone 5mg q4h and a lidoderm patch for pain. Her 
tachycardia, which was initially to the 150s, had been stable 
for at least 24h at time of transfer. She had a transaminitis on 
admission that improved. She was ambulating and tolerating po 
intake, and her pain was under control. She has a normocytic 
anemia thought to be secondary to the effect of acetaminophen on 
the bone marrow or kidneys, and which will need outpatient 
follow-up with either the liver clinic or her PCP.  
.
Upon admission, pt is tearful and endorses depressed mood since 
___. Prior to ___, she was living with her boyfriend in 
___ and working as a ___. She cannot identify anything that 
triggered the onset of these symptoms, and has never experienced 
any similar symptoms before. Her depressed mood has been 
associated with disrupted sleep (difficulty falling asleep and 
unwillingness to get out of bed in the morning), anhedonia, and 
poor concentration. Her appetite has remained normal. She saw a 
psychiatrist who prescribed celexa 40mg (not effective), prozac 
(too agitated) and subsequently effexor (some improvement in 
symptoms, but apparently stopped when she got sick). She had 
trouble focusing at work and eventually took a leave of absence 
for depression. 
.
In the setting of her depression, she had several new stressors. 
In ___, she developed abdominal pain and had surgery for 
endometriosis. Her boyfriend of ___ years, with whom she lived, 
ended their relationship in ___. She moved in with a 
roommate and then later returned home to live with her mother.  
While
intoxicated and upset, she engaged in disorderly contact (threw 
things at his house) and legal charges were filed against her. 
Her court date is pending in ___ and she was mandated 
to get a mental health evaluation (planning to go to partial 
hospitalization at ___ but unable to follow through). In
___, she got a tonsillectomy and unintentionally took too 
much acetaminophen, and she was hospitalized for acute liver 
failure and pancreatitis. She was hospitalized again in ___ 
for abdominal pain secondary to endometriosis vs. a hemorrhagic 
cyst.  After being discharged, she continued to have pain as 
well as persistent depressive symptoms. She states that her most 
recent overdose was ""semi-intentional"" and ""impulsive;"" she did 
not plan to end her life, but she wanted to make herself feel 
less. She states that she feels guilty about ""doing this to 
myself."" She denies SI and endorses feeling hopeful about her 
treatment and her future (going back to work, getting her life 
back).

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient is a ___ year-old female with endometriosis, hx of 
alcohol and narcotics abuse, and multiple recent medical 
complications and admissions s/p prior tylenol overingestion, 
who was transferred from ICU/medicine following an intentional
overdose of morphine.  Her depression comes in the context of a 
recent break up with boyfriend of ___ ___, medical leave from her 
job as ___, legal stressors ___ alcohol induced violent 
behaviors, relocation to ___ from ___, and multiple medical 
problems and pain.  During her hospital stay here, patient was 
cooperative with staff and peers, engaged in all groups and with 
her treatment team, and remained motivated for ongoing 
treatment.  She demonstrated marked improvement with her insight 
into her depression, contributing factors, and her tendency to 
""reach for something,"" whether that be pills or alcohol.  
Regarding her mood, it continued to slowly improve further every 
day, especially on days when she had a good night sleep.  She 
remained on a dose of 15 mg of Mirtazapine for depressed mood 
and improved sleep.  She denied suicidal thoughts during her 
stay here.  For sleep and mood stabilization, we began Seroquel 
50 mg at night and titrated up to a dose of 300 mg QHS and 50mg 
daily, which the patient responded to well.  She did not have 
any side effects of hypotension, dizziness, or oversedation.  
Regarding her abdominal pain, it also improved over the course 
of her stay here.  She tolerated a taper of narcotics, and pain 
was well controlled with standing ibuprofen and lidocaine 
patches; and neurontin. Her LLQ pain rated a ___ on day of 
discharge.  She appears safe and appropriate for discharge to 
partoal program and eager to engage in more intensive group 
therapy at her partial program. She no longer presented as an 
acute risk to herself.  
.

.
